_help: Scoring settings. Every pick is judged by how your team does once the draft is complete: your pick's own effect (map strength, counters against enemies already picked, pairs with allies already picked) plus how the rest of the draft goes after it, played out pick by pick with each side taking its best option. All in win-rate points (+1 = one percentage point). See README > Scoring.

simulation._help: Playing out the rest of the draft after your pick, so earlier picks account for what comes next. Each remaining pick goes to the side that owns it, which takes the brawler worth most to it: strength on the map plus how it pairs with its team and matches up against the other. Other players pick from brawlers actually played on this map (picked in at least minPickRate of its games). Your pick's pairs with your likely teammates count teammateWeight as much, since solo-queue teammates don't always pick what fits you. Enemies don't always pick the best answer either: each enemy pick still to come is a spread over what they might take, starting from how often each brawler is picked on this map (the meta) and tilted toward picks that suit the board. A pick worth x more on this board (in win-rate fractions, 0.1 = 10 points) is e^(answerFocus * x) times as likely: at 100, a 3-point counter is 20 times as likely as usual and a 1-point edge 2.7 times. 100 keeps counter risk about where it was before the meta weighting; lower values (enemies mostly pick what's popular) make first and last picks MORE alike. A placeholder until it can be fitted from real picks.

_synergyWeight: How much teammate pairs count: pairs with allies already picked, with your likely teammates, and in the other players' predicted picks. Set by the backtest (npm run backtest): on Nov 6 and Nov 7 games, the weight that predicted results best was 0.33 and 0.51, and 0.5 beat 1 on both days. Map strength and matchups fitted at about 1, so they have no weight of their own.

smoothing._help: Bayesian smoothing strength for win rates, in games. Higher = trust thin data less. Each level is pulled toward the level above it: map -> mode -> all modes -> 50%. (Matchups and pairs don't use these: they're shrunk by empirical Bayes, fitted from all pairs in the data.)

carryover._help: How much of a brawler's edge elsewhere is assumed to carry over before this map's own games say otherwise. 1 = all of it, 0 = none (start from 50%). A brawler that wins on close-range maps may lose on long-range ones, and rarely picked brawlers' win rates are inflated by specialists, so neither is trusted fully.

uncertainty._help: How much to prefer proven picks over promising but unproven ones. The 'unproven' part subtracts this many standard errors of the map win rate, so a brawler with no games on the map loses ~3 points and one with 2,000 games loses ~1. 0 turns it off.

roles._help: Role fit, in win-rate fractions (0.01 = 1 point). fill: per role your team doesn't have yet (max 2). duplicate: per role it already has. answer: per role that answers a role on the enemy team.
